headline: Study reports pairwise judging can recover capability signals from saturated benchmark transcripts
summary: Hamada, Yeon, Migliarini, Olive and Dubois evaluate whether correctly solved transcripts from saturated benchmarks retain information about model capability on harder items. In a retrospective study covering 16 target models across science, mathematics, coding and cybersecurity, the authors report that pairwise LLM judging predicts held-out capability better than a score-only baseline. Its pooled mean squared prediction error is 0.26 versus 1.37 for baseline assignment (a reported 5.27-fold reduction), but performance varies across domains and time: the method fails to beat baseline in some historical periods and substantially underestimates the first reasoning models. The work is a paper-reported evaluation method, not an independently validated safety assessment.
